extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of political philosophy; rulers, clergy, and legislators
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts of Hobbes' Leviathan presenting normative standards for civil authority, law, and religion — identifying doctrines, errors, and procedural rules Hobbes uses to evaluate governments and ecclesiastical power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure of Good and Evill in a Commonwealth
rubrics_metrics.description: Not the Appetite of Private men, but the Law, which is the Will and Appetite of the State is the measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge the goodness or wickedness of actions by public law rather than private passions; private measures of good are vain and pernicious to the public state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lawfull Marriage Is Not Unchastity
rubrics_metrics.description: It is vain and false philosophy to say the work of Marriage is repugnant to Chastity, or Continence, and by consequence to make them Morall Vices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat lawful marriage as inherently sinful; prohibitions of clerical marriage are rooted in ecclesiastical design for power, not moral necessity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Against Branding All Non-Popular Government as Tyranny
rubrics_metrics.description: From Aristotles Civill Philosophy they call all manner of Common-wealths but the Popular ... Tyranny; but 'Tyrant' originally signified a Monarch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid pejorative labels based on partial tradition; recognize that arbitrary names (tyranny, oligarchy, anarchy) are often expressions of popular anger rather than careful political judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: That Not Men, But Law Governs (critique)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aristotle's doctrine that in a well ordered common-wealth not men should govern, but the Laws, is an error — laws require the hands and swords of men to execute them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that the authority of law depends on men and force; rhetorical appeal to 'law alone' can mislead and encourage revolt if people ignore the material means that enforce law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laws Should Not Extend Over Conscience and Private Thought
rubrics_metrics.description: It is an error to extend the power of the Law... to the very Thoughts, and Consciences of men, by Examination, and Inquisition of what they Hold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Civil magistrates may require conformity of speech and action for certain public offices, but forcing self-accusation or punishing unexpressed opinions violates natural law; punishment of thought alone is unjust unless actions are forbidden by law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private Interpretation of Law Is Erroneous
rubrics_metrics.description: For a Private man, without the Authority of the Common-wealth... to Interpret the Law by his own Spirit, is another Error in the Politiques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation and explanation of law belong to the sovereign authority; unauthorized private exegesis (including of scriptures where they are law) undermines civil order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of Language; reject scholastic obscurity
rubrics_metrics.description: The Writings of Schoole-Divines are... insignificant Traines of strange and barbarous words... which hide the Truth, and make men think they have it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer plain, intelligible language; obscure scholastic jargon that cannot be rendered intelligible into modern tongues is likely hiding error or preventing further inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject Doctrines Based Solely on Fictitious Miracles or Tradition
rubrics_metrics.description: All the Legend of fictitious Miracles, in the lives of the Saints; and all the Histories of Apparitions, and Ghosts... have no warrant, neither in Reason, nor Scripture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat traditions and miracle-stories with skepticism; evaluate testimony critically, especially when Fathers' accounts rest on rumor rather than demonstrable fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oppose Suppression of Reason and Inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: With the Introduction of False, we may joyn also the suppression of True Philosophy, by such men... that have supposed such Doctrine... have been punished for it by Authority Ecclesiasticall.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow philosophical and natural inquiry to be examined by competent judges; silence or punishment is only justified under civil law if teaching causes disobedience, sedition, or breaches public peace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cui Bono — Assess Author by Who Benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: He That Receiveth Benefit By A Fact, Is Presumed To Be The Author... amongst Praesumptions, there is none that so evidently declareth the Author, as doth the BENEFIT of the Action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When investigating the origin or purpose of doctrines or institutions, look to whose worldly interests and benefits they serve as a primary presumption of authorship or motive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate Doctrines by Their Worldly Consequences (Church Militant critique)
rubrics_metrics.description: That The Present Church Now Militant On Earth, Is The Kingdome Of God... are annexed these worldly Benefits... the Pastors... are entitled... to a Right of Governing the Church; and consequently... to be Rectors, and Governours of the Common-wealth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be skeptical of doctrinal claims that place the church as an already-fulfilled kingdom of God when they produce clear secular advantages (power, exemption, revenues) for clergy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Papal Infallibility as Means to Enforce Obedience
rubrics_metrics.description: That the Pope In His Publique Capacity Cannot Erre... who beleeving this to be true, will not readily obey him in whatsoever he commands?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify doctrines of absolute religious authority as mechanisms to secure obedience; treat assertions of infallibility as politically consequential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subjection of Bishops to the Pope (foreign ecclesiastical dependency)
rubrics_metrics.description: That all other Bishops... have not their Right... but from the Pope, is a Doctrine, by which there comes to be... many potent men... that have their dependance on the Pope, and owe obedience to him, though he be a forraign Prince.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that ecclesiastical chains of dependence can create avenues for foreign political interference and civil unrest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions of the Clergy From Civil Law
rubrics_metrics.description: The exemption of these, and of all other Priests, and of all Monkes, and Fryers, from the Power of the Civill Laws... pay no part of the Publique expence; nor are lyable to the penalties, as other Subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat legal exemptions for clergy as politically and fiscally significant: they create privileged classes not accountable to civil authority and undermine public order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Priestly Titles and Sacrificial Language to Legitimize Power
rubrics_metrics.description: The giving to their Priests... the name of Sacerdotes, that is, Sacrificers... Also, the making the Lords Supper a Sacrifice, serveth to make the People beleeve the Pope hath the same power over all Christian, that Moses and Aaron had over the Jews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch for religious language and ritual redefinitions that equate clerical roles with ancient sovereign-sacral authority—these function to confer secular power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sacramentation of Marriage as Control over Succession
rubrics_metrics.description: The teaching that Matrimony is a Sacrament, giveth to the Clergy the Judging of the lawfulnesse of Marriages; and thereby, of what Children are Legitimate; and consequently, of the Right of Succession to haereditary Kingdomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify sacramental control of marriage as mechanism for clerical influence over inheritance and political succession.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial of Marriage to Priests as Political Strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Deniall of Marriage to Priests, serveth to assure this Power of the pope over Kings. For if a King be a Priest, he cannot Marry, and transmit his Kingdome to his Posterity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret clerical celibacy rules in light of political effects on dynastic succession and sovereign independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auricular Confession as Intelligence for Ecclesiastical Power
rubrics_metrics.description: From Auricular Confession, they obtain, for the assurance of their Power, better intelligence of the designs of Princes, and great persons in the Civill State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat private confession practices as potential channels for gathering politically sensitive information, reinforcing ecclesiastical leverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonization and Martyr-Declaring to Cement Resistance to Civil Authority
rubrics_metrics.description: By the Canonization of Saints, and declaring who are Martyrs, they assure their Power, in that they induce simple men into an obstinacy against the Laws and Commands of their Civill Soveraigns even to death.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that sanctifying individuals can create durable oppositional loyalties that impede civil governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transubstantiation, Penance, and Absolution as Instruments of Power
rubrics_metrics.description: They assure the same, by the Power they ascribe to every Priest, of making Christ; and by the Power of ordaining Pennance; and of Remitting, and Retaining of sins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat doctrines giving clerics authority over souls and absolution as political tools for compliance and control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purgatory, Indulgences, and External Works Enrich Clergy
rubrics_metrics.description: By the Doctrine of Purgatory, of Justification by externall works, and of Indulgences, the Clergy is enriched.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify soteriological doctrines that tariff spiritual benefit for payment as mechanisms for clerical enrichment and influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Daemonology and Exorcism as Means to Inspire Awe
rubrics_metrics.description: By their Daemonology, and the use of Exorcisme... they keep (or thinke they keep) the People more in awe of their Power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be wary of religious practices that exploit fear of spirits or miracles to consolidate authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: School-Divinity (Scholasticism) Protects Error
rubrics_metrics.description: The Metaphysiques, Ethiques, and Politiques of Aristotle, the frivolous Distinctions, barbarous Terms, and obscure Language of the Schoolmen... serve them to keep these Errors from being detected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat scholastic complexity and technicalities as possible intentional obfuscation that preserves institutional power; demand clearness and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power Is Preserved by Virtue, Not by Suppression
rubrics_metrics.description: Power is preserved by the same Vertues by which it is acquired; that is to say, by Wisdome, Humility, Clearnesse of Doctrine, and sincerity of Conversation; and not by suppression of the Naturall Sciences... nor by obscure Language... nor by Pious Frauds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rulers and pastors should sustain authority through wisdom, humility, clear teaching, and honest conduct rather than by coercion, secrecy, or fraud.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method to Dissolve Ecclesiastical Power (reverse the knots)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Analysis, or Resolution is by the same way; but beginning with the knot that was last tyed... First, the Power of the Popes was dissolved totally by Queen Elizabeth... After this, the Presbyterians... obtained the putting down of Episcopacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To dismantle an entrenched composite power, undo its constituent legal/institutional steps in reverse order from the most recent to the oldest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contraints on Rebellion: Laws, Force, and War
rubrics_metrics.description: Without such Arbitrary government, such Warre must be perpetuall; and that it is Men, and Arms, not Words, and Promises, that make the Force and Power of the Laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that the breakdown of sovereign enforcement leads to perpetual conflict; evaluation of political action must account for the material means that maintain peace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to a Conqueror: Point of Submission
rubrics_metrics.description: The point of time, wherein a man becomes subject of a Conquerour, is that point, wherein having liberty to submit to him, he consenteth, either by expresse words, or by other sufficient sign... that for him that hath no obligation to his former Soveraign but that of an ordinary Subject, it is then, when the means of his life is within the Guards and Garrisons of the Enemy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A subject's obligation to a new sovereign begins when he validly consents (expressly or by sufficient sign), typically when the enemy effectively controls the means of life and offers the liberty to submit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconciliation of Contrary Faculties by Education and Discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: From the contrariety of some of the Naturall Faculties of the Mind... Judgment, and Fancy may have place in the same man; but by turnes... For by Education, and Discipline, they may bee, and are sometimes reconciled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess persons and institutions by their ability to cultivate and order diverse faculties (reason, eloquence, courage) through education and discipline so they serve civil ends.
